resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1935 newspaper already describes the tower; a Flickr postcard caption says a tower 'built with inside stairs in 1939'. The story reports both and does not pick a build year.

A Pinterest pin caption says the tower burned down; the family email (2017) says it was taken down and only foundations remain. The story follows the family account, which is more detailed and points to a dated 2015 photo, and reports the disagreement.

notes_for_editor: Name and area rest on the Forest Lookouts clippings (1935-1937) and the OSM point at 44.856, -84.317. No second source confirms the exact spot, so check the OSM point against a Montmorency County or Michigan DNR map before relying on it. The fate account is one family email dated 30 April 2017, a personal recollection, and it is the only source for the dismantling. The OSM point still carries tower tags, so it is stale. Brief status 'unknown' is replaced with 'removed' on that email's account. The 1937 article gives 341 climbers for the Comstock tower. Its opening line's 'nearly 350' refers to 'one tower alone', which probably is a busier tower, since the article contrasts the Comstock tower with it as far off the most traveled highways; the story uses 341 only.
